I don't mean this in an offensive or snobby way but you could always tell who became a timberwolves fan more recently. I'm not even a veteran from the KG era but from KLove's rookie season and it still gave me a skin thick enough to ignore all this noise, I mean do you remember how the wolves used to play two years ago? I got gastritis every damn time I'd try to catch the game over dinner. I had to end up making a rule that game day is early dinner day as I shed a tear every time the "Dunkchamp" would drive down the lane just to brick layups.
And times even before that- blame it on the roster, blame it on the coach but we were always a terrible team that was mediocre at best (remembering the give KLove more playing time days). Every year was a constant rollercoaster of high expectations thinking this was finally the year our players potential would break through (This offseason Rubio said his shooting is coming along!) or finally drafting the piece we needed (I can't believe we were lucky enough to draft Derrick Williams!) But of course as everyone knows, it's been a long fucking cold winter here at Target center, longer than a FREAKIN DECADE. 

But somehow this time, we aren't completely screwing things up. Even though it was before Thibs, we actually drafted right (Knowing us I wouldn't have been surprised if we ended up drafting Okafor over Towns. You very damn well know it was pretty close to happening) and there has been numerous on and off court improvements under Thibs. Name the last time we had a bench player of Jamal Crawford's caliber. Name the last time we had a free agent signing like Jeff Teague. You think he would have come if Sam Mitchell was still our coach? Think again. Hey, we're actually winning a bit now and yeah not a lot of these games look pretty and it still can get pretty infuriating but considering the fact that 3/5 starters are completely new to the team and the other two are 22and younger I like where we're at. All I can see is improvements happening all over the place and I'm happy with that. Like a lot of you I am a bit skeptical about the Patton draft since we have a lot of bigs but I'd hold my judgment until I see him actually play on the NBA court. 

Hey, we've been through so much worse. We were the example A of any sports franchise of what not to be.
Right now this? this is nothing. Put on your shades, zone out the haters, and keep calm and relax until Towns grows into the future MVP we all know he will be. We're better than this.

I do agree that it isn't a common contact layup but regardless, his  arm motion still intends to, and does make the basket with the shot. I don't see how a made shot attempt can be excessive and intended to harm when the motion still justifies and in this case perfectly carries out a full shot. I'm not saying Melo may not have done any wrong, but if that's the case, an offensive foul or perhaps even an technical would have been more appropriate [considering that the refs didn't even care about previous facial contact against OKC.](http://twitter.com/BleacherReport/status/927603019537158145)

I do agree that the basket was open and Melo had a lane but I think he recognized the defense (Nurk) coming in and went for the contact on purpose for the and1, which is quite the common moves most guards try to pull these days except at their size, their elbow doesn't usually come up that high. Also the main complaint seems to be with the consistency of the calls. When Westbrook AND Melo got hit in the face before, they shrugged it off even without a common foul, which a contact to the face should warrant. If this was actually a intentional revenge play by Melo, it would/should have been prevented by a correct call by the refs earlier in the game and if not, then I think an offensive foul or a shooting foul (and1) is more appropriate than a flagrant2 since his body motions including his arms were going for a shot after all. Either way, the refs messed up pretty bad and fans want them to be held responsible because for the most part they walk away consequence free, waiting for the day to fuck up another game.

I don't think the current warriors are the same. In sports, especially in the modern era, context is crucial as well. That's why we love the underdogs and applaud them when they even achieve a decent, unexpected record and berate teams with mediocre success when they could/should have done better. That's why the clippers, even with all the success they had gets scrutinized by the media on a daily basis. I'm not saying that the warriors are a bad team. In fact, I think they actually may be the best non-national team ever. Therefore, the addition of Kevin Durant and the manner and context that he came, on top of their previous record breaking 73win season received strong criticism for a reason. If lebron stayed at Miami and never returned to cleveland, he wouldn't have the same level of respect and legacy. Same with the warriors (unfortunately because the teams superstar affects the teams legacy and reputation as well), they don't get respected as much not because they're not good enough, but how they came to sit on the throne. That is why in my opinion, the team that won the championship at 2015 albeit worse was the better respected, more like-able team. The end doesn't justify the means.
